questions.q: Where does the story begin, as Father Wolf wakes up from his day's rest?
choices: In the Seeonee hills
Beside the Waingunga River
At the Council Rock
In a village rubbish-heap
questions.evidence: a very warm evening in the Seeonee hills

questions.q: Why do the wolves of India despise Tabaqui the jackal?
choices: He makes mischief, tells tales and eats rags from rubbish-heaps
He steals the wolves' kills and gives them to the tiger to eat
He hunts the wolf cubs whenever their parents are away
He breaks the Law of the Jungle by hunting cattle in the villages
questions.evidence: he runs about making mischief, and telling tales

questions.q: Why did Tabaqui praise the wolf cubs to their parents' faces?
choices: He knew it was unlucky and liked making the wolves uncomfortable
He hoped the wolves would let him live in the cave with them
He truly thought the cubs were the finest he had ever seen
He wanted Father Wolf to share the next night's hunt with him
questions.evidence: It pleased him to see Mother and Father Wolf look uncomfortable.

questions.q: Why did Mother Wolf say Shere Khan had only ever killed cattle?
choices: He was lame in one foot from birth
He was too old to chase deer
He was afraid of the wolf pack
He liked the taste of village cows
questions.evidence: He has been lame in one foot from his birth.

questions.q: According to the Law of the Jungle, what is the real reason beasts must not eat Man?
choices: Man-killing brings men with guns, gongs and torches, and then everyone suffers
Man is too clever to be caught, so hunting him wastes a whole night
Men are protected by the Pack Council and the wolves would punish the killer
Man's meat makes every beast in the jungle go mad with the dewanee
questions.evidence: man-killing means, sooner or later, the arrival of white men on elephants

questions.q: How did Shere Khan miss his prey and hurt himself?
choices: He jumped at a woodcutter's campfire and burned his feet
He fell into a hidden trap and cut his paw
He slipped on the riverbank and twisted his leg
He ran into a thorn bush and scratched his face
questions.evidence: jump at a woodcutter's campfire, and has burned his feet

questions.q: What did the baby do when he first looked up into Father Wolf's face?
choices: He laughed
He cried loudly for his mother
He ran back into the bushes
He hid behind a low branch
questions.evidence: He looked up into Father Wolf's face, and laughed.

questions.q: Shere Khan says, "My quarry. A man's cub went this way." What does "quarry" mean here?
choices: An animal or person being hunted
A place where stone is dug out
A meal shared with a friend
A gift owed to a leader
questions.evidence: My quarry. A man's cub went this way

questions.q: Why could Shere Khan not simply walk in and take the baby from the wolves?
choices: The cave mouth was too narrow for a tiger to come in
Tabaqui warned him that the whole Pack was hiding inside
His burned feet were too sore for him to climb up the hill
Baloo and Bagheera were guarding the cave entrance that night
questions.evidence: the mouth of the cave was too narrow for a tiger to come in by

questions.q: What did Mother Wolf, called Raksha the Demon, tell Shere Khan the man's cub would do in the end?
choices: Hunt Shere Khan himself
Lead the whole Seeonee Pack
Go back to live among men
Become Tabaqui's master

questions.q: Why did Mother Wolf choose the name Mowgli for the baby?
choices: It means the Frog
It means the Brave One
It was his human parents' name for him
It means Little Brother of the wolves
questions.evidence: for Mowgli the Frog I will call thee

questions.q: By the Law of the Jungle, why must a wolf bring his young cubs to the Pack Council?
choices: So the other wolves can identify them
So they can be given their hunting names
So the leader can pick the strongest ones
So they can learn the Law from Baloo
questions.evidence: in order that the other wolves may identify them

questions.q: What do we learn about Akela, the leader of the Pack?
choices: He had been trapped twice and beaten once, so he knew the ways of men
He was the youngest wolf ever to lead the Seeonee Pack by his strength
He was Shere Khan's old friend and often hunted beside the great tiger
He was Father Wolf's brother and had raised him from a little cub
questions.evidence: He had fallen twice into a wolf trap in his youth

questions.q: Why could Baloo the bear come and go as he pleased, even at the Pack Council?
choices: He eats only nuts, roots and honey
He is the oldest animal in the jungle
He is stronger than any wolf in the Pack
He once saved Akela's life in a fight
questions.evidence: he eats only nuts and roots and honey

questions.q: At the Council, what happened right after Baloo spoke for the man's cub?
choices: Bagheera dropped into the circle and offered a bull for him
Shere Khan leaped into the circle and tried to seize him
Mother Wolf sprang forward to fight the young wolves
Akela accepted Mowgli and sent the whole Pack home
questions.evidence: A black shadow dropped down into the circle.

questions.q: The wolves made "a clamor of scores of voices." What is a clamor?
choices: A loud noise of many people talking at once
A quiet whisper passed slowly from ear to ear
A long silence while everyone thinks hard
A song that the wolves sing at the full moon
questions.evidence: There was a clamor of scores of voices

questions.q: What one thing did Bagheera tell Mowgli he must never kill or eat, and why?
choices: Cattle, because he was bought into the Pack with a bull's life
Deer, because the Pack needed them for food in the long winter
Monkeys, because they are cousins of men and know their language
Fish, because Baloo said they belong to the River and its people
questions.evidence: he must never touch cattle because he had been bought into the Pack at the price of a bull's life

questions.q: What is this part of the story mostly about?
choices: How a lost man's cub was saved and accepted into the wolf pack
How the wolves drove Shere Khan away from the Seeonee hills forever
How Tabaqui the jackal went mad and attacked the wolves' cave
How Mowgli learned to hunt and later became leader of the Pack
questions.evidence: And that is how Mowgli was entered into the Seeonee Wolf Pack
